title: Holter ECG for children
what: Sensors are stuck on your child's chest, and a small device records their ECG for 24 hours. Your child goes about a normal day.
why: When a child has a racing heart, fainting, or chest pain, or the doctor heard skipped beats.
duration: usually worn for 24 hours; results come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: What exactly bothers your child, and when
If your child is allergic to bandages

prepare.title: Bathing
prepare.text: Bathe your child the day before. They cannot wash with the device on.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A loose undershirt or T-shirt, so the wires do not get in the way.

prepare.title: Talk about it
prepare.text: Explain to your child that the sensors must not be touched or pulled off.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down what your child did and felt: play, sleep, and complaints.

steps: The nurse cleans the skin on your child's chest
A small device on a belt or strap is connected to them
Your child goes home and lives as usual
You keep a diary: sleep, play, complaints
After 24 hours, the device is removed at the clinic
feel: Little ones sometimes grab the wires. Keep an eye on them
after: Results usually come in 1 to 3 days
Mild redness from the pads goes away on its own
Your doctor will explain the result
red_flags: Your child faints: call emergency services
Severe chest pain or shortness of breath

faq.q: Can my child run around with the Holter?
faq.a: Yes. Normal activity is actually needed. But no water and no swimming pool.

faq.q: What if a sensor comes off?
faq.a: Press it back on and write down the time. If it came off completely, call the clinic.

reminders.text: Your child's Holter goes on tomorrow. Give them a bath today and get a loose T-shirt ready.
